original_question: Given a variety X, a line bundle L on X, and an integer r, determine whether there exists a 0-dimensional subscheme X ⊆ X that is a disjoint union of degree-2 schemes such that the reduced subscheme X_red imposes independent conditions on L while X itself does not.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly identifies the ambient data (a variety X, a line bundle L on X, and an integer r), the existential nature of the question, the search for a 0-dimensional nonreduced scheme built from degree-2 pieces, the use of the reduced subscheme X_red, and the contrast between the reduced scheme imposing independent conditions on L while the full nonreduced scheme does not. Those are exactly the ingredients of Section 1.1, Problem 3.
missing_details: The paper-wide convention is that the ambient field is C: the notation section says the notes mainly work over complex numbers unless stated otherwise.
To make the question stand-alone and unambiguous, the 0-dimensional subscheme should be renamed (for example, Z ⊆ X) rather than reusing X for both the ambient variety and the subscheme.
The role of r should be made explicit: Z should be a union of r pairwise disjoint degree-2 subschemes, so deg(Z)=2r and deg(Z_red)=r.
The phrase "imposes independent conditions on L" should be defined exactly as dim H^0(X, I_Z ⊗ L)=max{dim H^0(X,L)-deg(Z),0}.
It should be stated explicitly that Z_red means the reduced subscheme underlying Z.

A faithful stand-alone version should not add hypotheses that are not in Problem 3: there is no generic-support assumption, no smoothness assumption on X, and no extra homogeneity, polynomial-degree, operator, or nilpotency condition in this problem.
The nearby context explains that the restriction to degree-2 components is the tractable specialization relevant to Terracini loci; keeping that restriction explicit is part of the paper's intent.
refined_question: Working over C, let X be a variety, let L be a line bundle on X, and let r >= 1. Determine whether there exists a zero-dimensional subscheme Z ⊆ X that is the union of r pairwise disjoint degree-2 subschemes (equivalently, deg(Z)=2r and deg(Z_red)=r) such that the reduced subscheme Z_red imposes independent conditions on L, namely dim H^0(X, I_{Z_red} ⊗ L)=max{dim H^0(X,L)-r,0}, while Z itself does not impose independent conditions on L, i.e. dim H^0(X, I_Z ⊗ L) > max{dim H^0(X,L)-2r,0}?
justification: The draft matches Section 1.1, Problem 3 essentially verbatim, so that is the exact target in the paper. To make it fully stand-alone, I imported two pieces of nearby context that Problem 3 relies on: the paper-wide convention that the notes work over complex numbers, and the precise cohomological definition of "imposes independent conditions" from the paragraph immediately before Problem 2. I also made explicit how the parameter r enters the problem: since the scheme is a union of degree-2 components and r is part of the input, the natural stand-alone sharpening is to say there are r such disjoint components, hence total degree 2r and reduced degree r. I did not broaden the problem to arbitrary fat-point schemes or add genericity assumptions, because the surrounding discussion instead emphasizes the degree-2 specialization and its connection to Terracini loci. The paper does not give a general equivalent reformulation of Problem 3, only special-case comments (for example, curves when r=2), so no alternate formulation is supplied.
